text: A simple binding knot like a shoelace bow is essentially two crossings of the two ends. The only thing that separates a square (reef) knot from a granny knot is the handedness of the second crossing: if it mirrors the first crossing you get a square knot that seats flat and holds, and if it repeats the first you get a granny that capsizes and slips. Most people whose laces keep coming undone are unknowingly tying a granny bow.
title: aadhar.sh: knots

text: The standard shoelace bow is cross, loop, wrap, pull. If the starting cross and the wrapping loop go the same way, the result is a granny bow that sits diagonally across the shoe and works loose. Reversing just one of the two steps gives a square bow that sits straight across the shoe and stays tied. Same moves, opposite handedness on the second step.
title: aadhar.sh: knots

text: The Ian knot, from Ian Fieggen, is a speed method that lands on the same knot as the standard bow, not a different knot. You form a loop in each hand at the same time and pass them through each other in one motion, instead of making one loop and wrapping the other lace around it. Tied with the correct handedness it produces the same square bow, just much faster. Ian's Secure variant adds an extra tuck for laces that still wander.
title: aadhar.sh: knots

text: Bunny ears ties a shoelace by making both loops first and then knotting the two loops like ropes. It is easy to learn but just as prone to the granny trap: tying the two ears with the same handedness as the starting cross produces a granny bow. The knot does not care which method produced the two crossings; only their relative handedness decides whether it holds or slips.
title: aadhar.sh: knots

text: The whole shoelace problem reduces to one rule that runs from a reef knot on a sail to the bow on a shoe: make the two crossings oppose each other. Cross one way, then cross back the other way. Matching the handedness makes the knot slip; opposing it makes the knot hold. Everything else about the various methods is speed and style.
title: aadhar.sh: knots

text: A reef knot (square knot) is an ancient binding knot used to secure a rope or line around an object, tied by making two half-knots of opposite handedness, one left-over-right and the other right-over-left. It lies flat, which is why it was used to reef sails. It is not secure as a bend for joining two separate ropes, especially of different sizes, because it can capsize and spill under load.
title: Reef knot (Wikipedia)

text: The granny knot is a binding knot tied by making two half-knots of the same handedness. It is notorious for slipping or jamming and is generally considered inferior to the square (reef) knot, which differs only in reversing the handedness of the second half-knot. The granny is a common mistake when a square knot is intended, including in shoelace bows.
title: Granny knot (Wikipedia)
